data.name: Iakobos
data.gender_notes: Iakobos is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Greek 'Iakobos', meaning 'supplanter' or 'he who follows'. In the Bible, Iakobos is the name of the second son of Isaac and Rebecca, and the elder brother of Esau. Renamed 'Israel' after wrestling with an angel, Iakobos is a symbol of faith, perseverance, and divine protection. The name Iakobos carries the meaning “God's protector” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Iakobos usually hope their child will grow to embody god's protector and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing God's protection and the strength of faith.
data.etymology: Iakobos belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's protector.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Iakobos total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: יעקבוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם יעקבוס מקורו בשם העברי יעקב, שפירושו 'החלפת העקב' או 'תפיסת הבוהן', הנגזר מהמילה 'עקב' שפירושו 'עקב' או 'בוהן'. זהו שם חשוב במקרא, הנושא על ידי אחד האבות של עם ישראל, יעקב, ששמו שונה לישראל אחרי שמאבק עם המלאך. השם יעקבוס הוא גרסה יונית של השם יעקב, המשמשת בברית החדשה.

in_greek.name: Ιακωβος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιακωβος είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος יעקב, που σημαίνει 'αντικατάσταση της πτέρνας' ή 'αρπαγή'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ο Ιακωβος αναφέρεται ως ο αδελφός του Ιησού και ως ο ηγέτης της εκκλησίας στην Ιερουσαλήμ. Το όνομα αυτό έχει μεγάλη σημασία στην ιστορία της Εκκλησίας και της πνευματικής παράδοσης.

in_latin.name: Iacobus
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Iacobus is derived from the Hebrew name יעקב, meaning 'supplanting' or 'heel grabber'. This name is significant in the Bible, borne by one of the patriarchs of the Israelites, Jacob, whose name was changed to Israel after wrestling with an angel. The Latin form Iacobus is used in Christian tradition to refer to Saint James, one of Jesus' apostles and the leader of the church in Jerusalem.

in_english.name: Iakobos
in_english.long_meaning: The name Iakobos originates from the Hebrew name יעקב (Ya'aqov), meaning 'supplanting', 'heel grabber', or 'replacement'. This name is borne by Jacob, one of the patriarchs in the Bible, whose name was changed to Israel. In Christian tradition, Iakobos (or James) refers to one of Jesus' apostles and the leader of the church in Jerusalem. The name signifies spiritual transformation and leadership.

data.cultural_impact: Iakobos is a revered name in the Christian community, originating from the biblical account of the second son of Isaac and Rebecca, Jacob or Iakobos in the original Greek. The name has been carried throughout history by numerous saints, kings, and noteworthy figures, including St. Jacob of Serug, Jacob of Sarug, and Jacob of Edessa. The cultural significance of the name is deeply rooted in Judeo-Christian tradition, symbolizing steadfastness, perseverance, and cunning, as demonstrated by the biblical Jacob's journey to obtain the birthright, as well as his struggle with an angel and his renaming as 'Israel'.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, Iakobos is a powerful reminder of faith and the rewards that come from maintaining it, as demonstrated by the biblical narrative. The name signifies Jacob's struggle to remain steadfast in his belief in God, despite the trials and hardships that life presented. The name is also connected to the deeply spiritual concept of divine protection, exemplified by God's intervention throughout Jacob's life to keep him safe. Ultimately, the name Iakobos calls to mind the idea that through faith, perseverance, and divine intervention, one can overcome adversity and come out on the other side stronger and more spiritually enriched.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Iakobos, meaning "supplanter" or "deceiver" in Hebrew, was given to the biblical patriarch Jacob as a prophecy of his deceptive past and divine promise of a blessed future. In Christianity, this name symbolizes the human condition of deceit and God's redemptive grace.

biblical_reference.note: Refers to Saint James, one of Jesus' twelve apostles.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Born in Palestine around 1 AD, Iakobos is best known as one of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ. The name Iakobos carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
Iakobos is traditionally believed to have been the first bishop of Jerusalem and the author of the Epistle of James in the New Testament.

trends: Iakobos is a common name in the Christian world
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Iakobos remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Peter Iakobos from Jerusalem, Israel embodies the meaning of Iakobos - "God's protector". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
